subject: Literature
title: James Joyce's Ulysses on Trial
description: A quick win: understand James Joyce's Ulysses on Trial.

hook.text: The United States Postal Service burned copies of Ulysses for over a decade, declaring the novel legally obscene.

buildup.text: Joyce's revolutionary novel was serialized in a magazine, and the obscenity charge came from a single explicit chapter.

discovery.text: In 1933, Judge John Woolsey ruled that a book must be judged as a whole, not by isolated passages.

twist.text: Woolsey declared Ulysses 'a sincere and serious attempt to devise a new literary method,' making it legally art.

climax.text: The ruling established the legal principle that artistic merit can override obscenity charges in American courts.

punchline.text: A judge's ruling turned a banned book into a legal landmark.

quiz.question: What legal principle did the Ulysses trial establish?
options: All novels with sexual content must be banned
A book must be judged as a whole, and artistic merit can override obscenity charges
Only government-approved publishers can print novels
